instruction: Set VLC to always stay on top of other windows.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);
import subprocess; import time; subprocess.run(['pkill', 'vlc']); time.sleep(1);

metadata.explanation: Task requires the agent to enable the always-on-top setting in VLC so the window stays above other windows. The evaluator checks the VLC configuration file to verify the 'video-on-top' setting is enabled. Custom getter reads the VLC config file and extracts the always-on-top setting, and custom metric compares it against the expected enabled state.

llm_judge_reasons: Semantic verification is correct: Getter extracts 'video-on-top' setting from VLC config file, which directly corresponds to the always-on-top feature requested in the instruction
Coverage is complete: Instruction requires enabling always-on-top, and evaluator checks exactly this requirement
Metric logic is correct: Properly handles expected parameter (receives rules dict directly when type='rule') and compares result against expected.get('on_top_enabled', True)
Getter logic is sound: Returns False when 'video-on-top' not found in config, which is reasonable since agent must actively enable the setting for it to appear in config
Postconfig includes VLC shutdown (pkill vlc + 1 second sleep), which should trigger VLC to save config to disk before verification
Minor timing concern: 1-second sleep may not be sufficient on slower systems for VLC to complete writing config file
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider increasing postconfig sleep time to 2-3 seconds to ensure VLC has fully written config file on all systems
Optional: Add explicit verification that config file was modified after task execution (check file modification time)
